name: Todd Wanek
current_role: President & CEO, Ashley Furniture Industries (Arcadia, Wisconsin)
profile: Son of founder Ron Wanek, Todd Wanek has been CEO of Ashley Furniture since 2002, after running its Taiwan factory for five years and becoming COO in 1996. Ashley is the world's largest home furnishings manufacturer and North America's largest furniture store brand; his father remains chairman.
interesting_fact: As a teen and college student he worked odd jobs at Ashley, including on the production line and shipping furniture, and after college spent five years living in Asia managing the company's Taiwan factory.
deep_cut_fact: He was named a 2026 Tampa Bay Father of the Year by the National Father's Day Council (June 2026 luncheon benefiting Big Brothers Big Sisters). Ashley's Hope to Dream program, which he describes as starting to help local kids who needed a mattress, passed 200,000 donated beds.

public_contacts.value: Sharon Okaah, Flytevu - sharon.okaah@flytevu.com (campaign media contact on Ashley press release)

notes: Best route is Ashley corporate PR (publicrelations@ashleyfurniture.com). Hope to Dream bed-donation program is a good warm hook. Flytevu contact appears campaign-specific.

name: Divyank Turakhia
current_role: Dubai-based tech entrepreneur and investor; founder and former CEO of Media.net, co-founder of Directi
profile: Mumbai-born programmer who co-founded web-hosting/domain group Directi with brother Bhavin in 1998 at age 16, then built contextual-ad network Media.net, sold in 2016 to a Chinese consortium for $900M, one of the largest ad-tech deals ever. Now based largely in Dubai, he invests and builds new ventures.
interesting_fact: He was named India's youngest billionaire three years running (2016-2018) and the youngest self-made Gulf billionaire in 2017.
deep_cut_fact: He started coding at age eight; a 2021 interview with domain investor Mike Mann was titled 'From Wing Walking to Billion-Dollar Exits', and Entrepreneur India profiled his passion for flying planes and scuba diving.
notes: Low public profile; no verified personal social accounts or published office email found. Some web profiles about him are aggregator/AI-written; current title unverified. Don't confuse with brother Bhavin (Zeta, Flock).

name: Joan Tisch
profile: Died November 2, 2017 in Manhattan at age 90; widow of Preston Robert Tisch (Loews Corp. co-founder, NY Giants co-owner). Death announced by the New York Giants.
notes: Deceased (source: https://www.cbsnews.com/newyork/news/joan-tisch-dead ; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joan_Tisch). Her stake passed to children Steve, Jonathan and Laurie Tisch. Remove from outreach list.

name: Akihiko Otsuka
profile: Former chairman of Otsuka Holdings and longtime president of Otsuka Pharmaceutical (1976-2000). Died November 28, 2014, aged 77, while serving as representative director and chairman, per Otsuka Holdings' official notice.
notes: Deceased (source: Otsuka Holdings TSE disclosure https://www2.jpx.co.jp/disc/45780/140120141201087645.pdf ; https://www.yakuji.co.jp/?p=40292). Current chairman is Ichiro Otsuka. Remove from outreach list.

name: Bradley Jacobs
current_role: Chairman & CEO, QXO (building products distribution); also to be chairman & CEO of new acquisition platform CKX
profile: Serial roll-up builder: United Waste (sold 1997 for $1.9B), United Rentals, then XPO Logistics (2011), which he split into XPO, GXO and RXO. Since 2024 he has run QXO, buying Beacon Roofing, Kodiak ($2.25B) and TopBuild (~$17B, closed July 2026), aiming for $50B revenue; in Nov 2026 he announced a second $1B-backed platform, CKX.
interesting_fact: A trained classical pianist, he studied math and music at Brown before dropping out; he has written two books, 'How to Make a Few Billion Dollars' (2024) and a 2025 sequel.
deep_cut_fact: His first company was Amerex Oil Associates, an oil brokerage he co-founded in 1979 and ran until its 1983 sale; he then moved to London and founded oil trader Hamilton Resources, and often credits financier Ludwig Jesselson as a mentor.
notes: Very media-friendly (books, frequent interviews). Best route: QXO media contact Joe Checkler. New CKX platform's target industry undisclosed - possible podcast hook.

name: Rajeev Juneja
current_role: Vice Chairman & Managing Director, Mankind Pharma (New Delhi); President, PHD Chamber of Commerce and Industry (2025-26)
profile: Co-founded Mankind Pharma with elder brother Ramesh Juneja (company started 1991 with ~20 staff and INR 5M seed capital; incorporated 1995). Mankind sells affordable generics plus consumer brands (Manforce condoms, Prega News). He led its May 2023 IPO and the 2024 INR 13,630 crore acquisition of Bharat Serums and Vaccines.
interesting_fact: He and his younger brother were born on the same date, ten years apart; Amitabh Bachchan is Mankind's brand ambassador.
deep_cut_fact: He credits Mankind's growth to a 'startup culture' and the mantra of staying dynamic: 'In a fast-changing world, you cannot remain stationary... Every day is a new day.' He also said of the IPO: 'It makes you more responsible.'
notes: Also reachable via PHDCCI (industry chamber) in his presidency role. Company also lists investors@mankindpharma.com.

name: Alki David
current_role: Media/tech entrepreneur; founder of FilmOn and Hologram USA; shareholder in the Leventis-David group (Coca-Cola HBC)
profile: Lagos-born Cypriot-British heir to the Leventis-David trading family, whose holdings are tied to Coca-Cola HBC bottling. He founded internet-TV service FilmOn (2006), hologram-entertainment firm Hologram USA and other ventures, and acted in and directed independent films. No verified 2026 business activity found.
interesting_fact: He studied film at the Royal College of Art, acted in 'The Bank Job' (2008) and wrote/directed indie films such as 'Fishtales'.
deep_cut_fact: His father Andrew A. David joined the family's Leventis-David Group in Ghana in 1957 and managed a Coca-Cola bottling plant in Accra; in 1998 Alki co-founded London modelling agency Independent Models.
notes: HIGH REPUTATIONAL RISK: multiple civil sexual-misconduct judgments since 2019 (incl. a reported $900M jury award in 2024) and other legal issues per Wikipedia; in 2021 he called earlier billionaire claims 'complete fiction'. Journalist should vet carefully before any outreach. No published contact route found.

name: Henrik Mads Clausen
current_role: Shareholder of Danfoss A/S (no public executive or board role found)
profile: Born 1953, one of five children of Danfoss founder Mads Clausen and Bitten Clausen. He is listed as a direct owner of Danfoss alongside Clausen Controls A/S and the Bitten & Mads Clausen Foundation (largest shareholder). Danfoss, based in Nordborg, Denmark, makes drives, cooling, heating and power solutions, including for data centers.
interesting_fact: Danfoss was founded by his father Mads Clausen in 1933 in a farmhouse attic on the island of Als; the company now leads in energy-efficient cooling, drives and heat pumps.

public_contacts.value: lars.lohff@danfoss.com (Lars Grubak Lohff, Head of Media Relations, Danfoss)

notes: Very private; no public role. Family is represented on the Danfoss board by third-generation Mads Clausen and Mads-Peter Clausen - better interview targets for an energy/data-center podcast. Approach via Danfoss media relations.
